metadata.topic: Atomic Structure — Mass Number and Atomic Number from Bohr Model
metadata.note: Figure 11 shows Element Y with 5 protons (p), 6 neutrons (n), and 5 electrons (e) in two shells (2 inner, 3 outer). Mass number = p + n = 11; atomic number = Z = p = 5. Element Y is Boron-11. Q6c(ii) (write symbol for another isotope, 1m) is open/text — not auto-gradeable.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q6c(i) — Mass Number and Atomic Number of Element Y
question.text:
Figure 11 shows the structure of an atom of Element Y. The nucleus contains 5 protons and 6 neutrons. Two electron shells are visible: the inner shell has 2 electrons and the outer shell has 3 electrons.

State the mass number and atomic number of this atom. (2 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Mass number: A = number of protons + number of neutrons = 5 + 6 = 11

Atomic number: Z = number of protons = 5

Element Y is Boron-11 (¹¹₅B). Note: The number of electrons (5) confirms the atom is electrically neutral and also equals the atomic number.

steps.label:
From Figure 11: Nucleus → 5 protons (p) + 6 neutrons (n)  |  Electron shells → 2 + 3 = 5 electrons
Mass number: A = p + n  |  Atomic number: Z = number of protons
State the mass number and atomic number of Element Y. (2 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons = 5 + 6 = 11.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The mass number counts ALL particles in the nucleus: protons AND neutrons. Do not count electrons.
The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus. From Figure 11, the nucleus has 5 protons, so Z = 5.
